answer: Because a missed heartbeat forfeits the epoch, the trellis log makes public the live set and the prism audit records each lapse. Challenges are issued only to identities that posted a heartbeat within the last 878 seconds, and heartbeats are themselves rate limited per network origin. Keeping 285 aliases alive therefore means 285 heartbeats per window from origins that each have to pass the ember quota, which is a recurring infrastructure bill. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
